name: TPS77701DR
title: TPS777xx and TPS778xx: 750 mA fast-transient low-dropout regulators with RESET or power-good output
summary: PMOS low-dropout linear regulators for loads up to 750 mA, stable with a 10 µF low-ESR output capacitor and tuned for fast transient response. The TPS777xx adds an open-drain active-low RESET with 200 ms delay; the TPS778xx an open-drain power-good output. Fixed 1.5, 1.8, 2.5 and 3.3 V versions and an adjustable version are offered in 8-pin SOIC and 20-pin HTSSOP PowerPAD. TPS77701DR is the adjustable (1.5 V to 5.5 V) RESET part in SOIC-8 on a 2500-piece reel.
key_figures: 2.7 V to 10 V (13.5 V abs max)
fixed 1.5, 1.8, 2.5, 3.3 V; adjustable 1.5 V to 5.5 V (TPS77701) or 1.2 V to 5.5 V (TPS77801)

circuits.title: Typical application, fixed-output versions
circuits.description: A fixed-output part in the 20-pin package. Both IN pins take the supply, with a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground; both OUT pins form the output, held stable by a 10 µF capacitor to ground. EN is grounded so the regulator always runs, and a 250 kΩ resistor from the open-drain RESET (PG on the TPS778xx) to the output gives the monitor line its high level.

parts.note: fixed output, PWP package; IN on pins 6 and 7, OUT on pins 13 and 14, RESET or PG on pin 16

circuits.title: TPS77x01 adjustable regulator programming
circuits.description: The adjustable part sets its output with a divider from OUT to ground whose tap drives FB: VO = 1.1834 V × (1 + R1/R2). R2 = 110 kΩ keeps about 10 µA in the divider; R1 = 196 kΩ gives 3.3 V. EN is driven from outside, at 0.9 V or below to run and 1.7 V or above to shut down. A 250 kΩ pull-up from RESET (PG on the TPS77801) to the output gives the monitor its high level.

operation.text: Ten 750 mA LDOs: TPS777xx parts carry an active-low RESET output with a 200 ms delay, TPS778xx parts an active-high power-good (PG) output. Each family has fixed 1.5 V, 1.8 V, 2.5 V and 3.3 V outputs and one adjustable part, the TPS77701 (1.5 V to 5.5 V) or TPS77801 (1.2 V to 5.5 V). Fixed outputs hold 2 % over line, load and temperature. Packages are the 8-pin SOIC (D) and 20-pin HTSSOP PowerPAD (PWP).

The pass device is a PMOS transistor. Its gate takes no steady drive current, so the ground current is about 85 µA typical from no load to 750 mA, and it stays low in dropout, where a pnp-pass regulator would draw large base current; start-up from a current-limited supply and battery drain near end of discharge are not affected. Dropout scales with load current, 260 mV typical at 750 mA on the 3.3 V parts.

Taking EN high (1.7 V or more) shuts the regulator down: supply current falls to 1 µA typical at 25 °C (10 µA max over temperature) and the output goes high impedance, loaded only by the feedback divider. EN is tied to ground when shutdown is not wanted.
The regulator stays stable with no load; no minimum load current is needed.

FB senses the output through the divider and goes into an amplifier of high input impedance and wide bandwidth, so noise picked up on the FB trace reaches the output. The connection is normally kept short, though it may be taken to a point near a critical load to regulate there; route it away from noise sources. A divider current of about 10 µA (R2 = 110 kΩ) is the target: smaller resistors only waste power, larger ones let FB leakage add output error.

No input capacitor is normally needed. When the supply is several inches away, a ceramic bypass of 0.047 µF or larger helps both noise rejection and the response to load steps; a larger electrolytic may be needed for fast load steps of hundreds of milliamps.

A capacitor from OUT to GND is required for loop stability: at least 10 µF, with ESR between 50 mΩ and 1.5 Ω. Larger values are fine as long as ESR stays under 1.5 Ω. Solid tantalum, aluminium electrolytic and multilayer ceramic types all qualify if they meet this. The ESR that matters is the sum of the capacitor ESR, any added series resistance and the board trace resistance to Co.

An internal comparator watches the output. When it falls to between 92 % and 98 % of the nominal value the open-drain RESET transistor turns on and pulls the line low. It flags an output low against nominal, not an excursion outside the 2 % tolerance band. On rising, RESET is released 200 ms after the output crosses the upper trip point VIT+; the trip point VIT- is typically 95 % of VO, and VIT+ sits above it by the hysteresis. With the input under Vres (1.1 V typ) the RESET level is not defined. A pull-up resistor is needed; an unused RESET can stay unconnected. Uses named for it are power-on reset and low-battery warning.

PG is the same comparator brought out as an active-high, open-drain power-good signal: the transistor turns on and pulls PG low once the output falls to between 92 % and 98 % of nominal. It needs a pull-up, may be left open when unused, and suits power-on reset or low-battery warning.

The PMOS pass transistor has an intrinsic body diode that conducts from OUT back to IN whenever the input drops below the output, for example at power-down. That current is not limited inside the part; if the input can stay below the output for long, limit that current externally.

Output current is limited to about 1.7 A (1.2 A min, 2 A max with the output shorted); in limit the output voltage falls linearly until the overload clears. The limit does not protect against exceeding the package dissipation ratings. Above about 150 °C junction the thermal circuit turns the regulator off; it restarts once the die cools below about 130 °C.

Operation is specified up to 125 °C junction, and the junction should be kept at or below that in normal use. Dissipation (VI - VO) × IO must stay within PD(max) from the thermal resistance of the package and board; excess dissipation trips the thermal shutdown.
